newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks end sharply up as rate fears ease.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks end sharply up as rate fears ease.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks staged a healthy rebound on Monday, more than recouping last week's losses, but low turnover suggested many investors remained cautious on the near term outlook, brokers said.
The Hang Seng Index advanced 187.01 points, or 1.70 percent, to 11,212.60. Turnover, however, was unimpressive at HK$3.20 billion, compared with HK$3.35 billion on Friday.
"Last week, the market was discounting a larger rise in interest rates," said Kieran Hung, vice-president, institutional sales, at G.K. Goh Securities.

The market fell 1.2 percent last week, fearing that any stronger than expected rise in U.S. employment could prompt the Fed to raise rates aggressively from this month. Friday's job figures, though, were roughly in line with predictions.
"Because of the U.S. election, we are not expecting more than a 25-basis point hike," said Hung.

Despite Monday's gains, brokers said they were concerned about the trend in the U.S. long bond. "For the near term, the Hong Kong market looks fully valued given its high correlation to U.S. interest rates and the long bond yield," said Gary Wong, sales director at Vickers Ballas.

"But other factors such as earnings momentum, political sentiment, inflation in Hong Kong and, most importantly, the upswing in the Chinese economy all make Hong Kong look good on a longer term basis," Wong said.
Interest-rate sensitive property counters led the market, with the property sub-index rising 2.16 percent compared to the market's 1.70 percent.
The finance sector rose 1.86 percent, chiefly on buying of HSBC and Hang Seng Bank. H shares and utilities underperformed.
HSBC put on HK$2.50 to close at HK$134.00 on moderate turnover of HK$228.91 million.
Short positions in HSBC -- only 50,000 shares worth HK$6.7 million -- were taken up in the afternoon.
Hang Seng Bank put on HK$1.50 to HK$79.50. The counter is seen as the Hong Kong bank with the highest quality earnings, an analyst said.
Henderson Land was the best performing blue chip, rising HK$1.75, or 2.84 percent, to HK$61.50. The company will report its results for the year ended June 30 on Wednesday.
Sun Hung Kai Properties and Cheung Kong both advanced HK$1.50 to HK$76.00 and HK$55.75.
